mainTopic: Honest weights and measures: following local custom, market inspectors, fair weighing, and the sizes of scales.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching from the previous דף: משה's curses cover all twenty-two letters of the alphabet, more than his blessings do. The גמרא then goes back to the משנה about local measuring customs and gives a סימן listing the teachings that follow. A ברייתא learns from "איפה שלמה" and "אבן שלמה" that a seller must follow the local custom for leveling or heaping, and for exact balance or tipping the scale. The extra word "וצדק" adds that he may not switch methods even if he adjusts the price. רב יהודה מסורא reads the same פסוקים as a warning: cheating with unequal measures leaves you poor, and honesty brings wealth. Another ברייתא says market inspectors are appointed for measures but not for prices. The גמרא tells how קרנא taught the opposite of what שמואל told him, following רבי יצחק. Next come rules for weighing a ליטרא and its parts, and for giving only one tip of the scale per weighing. The amud ends with the required sizes of different scales and asks what the first, largest scale is used for. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The blessings and curses of משה span the alphabet
steps.stepSummary: The end of a teaching from the previous דף. משה's blessings run from the letter ו to the letter מ. His curses run from ו all the way around the alphabet to ה, which covers all twenty-two letters.
steps.simpleTranslation: [משה blessed them] from "And it shall be, if you will surely listen" until "to serve them." And he cursed them with twenty-two letters, from "And it shall be, if you will not listen" until "and no one will buy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that began on the previous דף. It shows how many letters of the alphabet are covered by משה's blessings and by his curses in דברים 28.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blessings start with ו (והיה) and end with מ (לעבדם), so they cover only a few letters. The curses start with ו (והיה) and end with ה (קנה), which goes around the whole alphabet and covers all twenty-two letters. So the curses are described as fuller than the blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it shall be". The opening word of both sections, starting with the letter ו.
"To serve them". The last word of the blessings, ending with the letter מ.
"Buyer". The last word of the curses, ending with the letter ה.

steps.whatToRemember: This closes the earlier discussion. From the next line on, the גמרא is back to the משנה about measuring customs.
steps.confusionAlert: The first line starts in the middle of a sentence. The beginning of this teaching, about משה blessing them, is on the previous דף.

phrases.english: from "And it shall be, if you will surely listen"
phrases.notes: דברים 28:1. This sentence started on the previous דף, describing how משה blessed them.

phrases.english: until "to serve them";
and he cursed them with twenty-two [letters]:
from "And it shall be, if you will not listen"
until "and no one will buy."
phrases.notes: דברים 28:68. קנה ends with ה, the letter right before ו, so going from ו around to ה covers all 22 letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִ״וְּהָיָה אִם שָׁמוֹעַ תִּשְׁמַע״, וְעַד ״לְעׇבְדָם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement begun on the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה's blessings cover the letters ו through מ. His curses cover all twenty-two letters, from ו around to ה.

steps.title: Back to the משנה, with a memory list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about local measuring customs. It then gives a list of key words to help remember the teachings that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: "A place where they are accustomed to measure with a large measure, etc." (Memory aid: one may not balance precisely; one may not heap; with market inspectors; with a ליטרא; three; ten; fulcrum; weights; from a leveler; thick; you shall not do; one shall not do.)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה about measuring customs and sets up the discussion to come. It is not ruling on anything yet. It is only listing headings to remember the next teachings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says to follow the local custom: a large measure or small ones, and leveling or heaping. The סימן is a string of key words, one from each teaching coming up, in order, so a learner can remember the sequence.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid made of key words
A litra, a unit of weight or measure

steps.confusionAlert: Do not try to find a law in the סימן itself. It is only a list of headings for the teachings that come next.

phrases.english: A place where they are accustomed to measure with a large [measure], etc.
(Memory aid: "one may not balance precisely," "and one may not heap,"
"with market inspectors," "and with a litra," "three," "and ten,"
"fulcrum," "weights," "from a leveler," "thick,"
"you shall not do," "one shall not do.")

steps.triggerLanguage: מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּהֲגוּ לָמוֹד בְּגַסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by going back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In measuring, one follows the local custom. Where people use a large measure, one may not switch to small ones.

steps.title: No changing the local custom of leveling or heaping
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "איפה שלמה" that a seller may not level where the custom is to heap, or heap where the custom is to level.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that one may not level in a place where they heap, and may not heap in a place where they level? The verse says: "A complete measure."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule about leveling and heaping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "A complete measure" means the measure people in that place consider complete. If the custom is to heap, a leveled measure is short. If the custom is to level, a heaped measure is not what buyers expect.

keyTerms.meaning: Level off the top of the measure
Heap the measure above its rim

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where [do we know] that one may not level
in a place where they heap,
and one may not heap in a place where they level?
The verse says: "A complete measure."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מוֹחֲקִין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁגּוֹדְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller must follow the local custom of leveling or heaping, because the פסוק says "איפה שלמה".

steps.title: No changing the custom even with a price adjustment
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that a seller may not change the custom even if he offers to lower or raise the price to match. This is learned from the extra word "וצדק".
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he says, "I will level in a place where they heap and lower the price," or "I will heap in a place where they level and raise the price," we do not listen to him? The verse says: "A complete and honest measure you shall have."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. Even a fair price trade does not allow the seller to break the local custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the problem was only cheating, so fixing the price would solve it. The extra word "וצדק" teaches that the measure itself must be done the honest, local way, whatever the price.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not listen to him

steps.whatToRemember: The local measuring custom is required twice over. A seller may not change it at all ("שלמה"), and he may not change it even with a fair price trade ("וצדק").
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that honest measures are not only about the final money being fair. The way of measuring itself must follow what people expect.

phrases.english: And from where [do we know] that if he said:
"I will level in a place where they heap
and lower the price for him,"
or "I will heap in a place where they level
and add to the price for him,"
that we do not listen to him?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֵיפָה שְׁלֵמָה וָצֶדֶק יִהְיֶה לָּךְ״.
phrases.english: The verse says: "A complete and honest measure you shall have."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אָמַר: הֲרֵינִי מוֹחֵק בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁגּוֹדְשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 3 by covering the case where the seller offers a fair price trade.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even with a matching price adjustment, a seller may not change the local custom of leveling or heaping. This is learned from "וצדק".

steps.title: A seller may not change the local custom for weighing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "אבן שלמה" that where the custom is to let the scale tip, you may not balance it exactly, and where the custom is to balance it exactly, you may not let it tip.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: How do we know that you may not balance the scale exactly where people let it tip, and may not let it tip where people balance it exactly? The פסוק says: "A perfect weight."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that does for weights what the earlier ברייתא did for measures. You must weigh the way the local custom weighs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some places weigh so the scale is perfectly level. Other places let the scale tip down a bit, which gives the buyer a little extra. "אבן שלמה" teaches that a weight counts as 'perfect' only if it matches the custom of that place, so the seller may not switch methods.

keyTerms.meaning: Balancing the scale so it is exactly level
Letting the scale tip down, giving the buyer a little extra
"A perfect weight": the weight must match the local standard
"The פסוק teaches": introduces the source in the פסוק

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know that one may not balance the scale exactly
in a place where they let the scale tip,
and that one may not let it tip in a place where they balance it exactly?
The verse says: "A perfect weight."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְעַיְּינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Does for weights what step 3 did for measures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller must weigh according to the local custom, whether that is exact balance or tipping. Source: "אבן שלמה".

steps.title: Changing the weighing custom is not allowed even with a price adjustment
steps.stepSummary: Even if the seller offers to lower or raise the price to make up for weighing differently, we do not listen to him. This is learned from "וצדק".
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that if a seller says, "I'll balance exactly where people let it tip, and lower the price," or "I'll let it tip where people balance exactly, and raise the price," we don't listen to him? The פסוק says: "A perfect and just weight."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes one step further. Even a 'fair' trade, where the price is adjusted to match, is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think there is no problem if the price makes up for the difference in weight. The extra word "וצדק" (just) teaches that the honest way is to weigh exactly as the place weighs, with no switching at all. This matches step 4 about measures.

keyTerms.meaning: "I hereby": the seller announcing what he will do
We do not listen to him; his offer is not accepted

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he said:
"I will balance exactly, in a place where they let it tip,
and I will lower the price for him,"
or "I will let it tip, in a place where they balance exactly,
and I will add to the price for him,"
that we do not listen to him?
The verse says: "A perfect and just weight."

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן שֶׁאִם אָמַר: הֲרֵינִי מְעַיֵּין בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁמַּכְרִיעִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter rule on top of step 5, matching step 4 about measures
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller may not change the weighing method even if he adjusts the price to match. Source: "וצדק".

steps.title: Using two different measures leaves your house empty
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מסורא reads "לא יהיה לך בביתך" as a warning that you will have nothing at home, because you used "איפה ואיפה", two different measures.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה מסורא said: "You will not have in your house." Why? Because of "a measure and a measure," meaning two different measures.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה מסורא gives a new reading of the פסוק. He turns a ban into a warning about what will happen to a cheater.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק simply says not to keep two different measures in your house. רב יהודה splits the words. "לא יהיה לך בביתך" means you will end up with nothing in your house, and the reason is "איפה ואיפה": you cheated with unequal measures.

keyTerms.meaning: "A measure and a measure": two unequal measures, one large and one small

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda of Sura said:
"You will not have in your house"
phrases.notes: From דברים כה:יד. He reads these words on their own, as a warning: you will end up with nothing at home.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because of "a measure and a measure" (two different measures).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה מִסּוּרָא: לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ בְּבֵיתְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the halachic rules to a lesson about what happens to a cheater
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who uses unequal measures will end up with nothing in his house.

steps.title: Two different weights empty your purse, but honest ones bring wealth
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה מסורא reads "לא יהיה לך בכיסך" the same way, because of "אבן ואבן". Then he reads "יהיה לך" as a promise: honest weights and measures bring you wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: "You will not have in your purse." Why? Because of "a weight and a weight," two different weights. But "a perfect and just weight you shall have, a perfect and just measure you shall have."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה uses the same reading for weights and the purse. Then he ends with the good side: honesty brings wealth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning in דברים כה:יג is read like step 7. A cheater's purse will be empty. The next פסוק (כה:טו) says "יהיה לך", and he reads this as a promise: if your weights and measures are honest, you will have plenty.

keyTerms.meaning: "A weight and a weight": two unequal weights
"You shall have": read here as a promise of wealth

steps.whatToRemember: הלכה: weigh and measure exactly by the local custom, with no switching even for a price adjustment ("שלמה" and "וצדק"). Lesson: cheating with unequal weights and measures leads to poverty, and honesty leads to wealth.

phrases.english: "You will not have in your purse"
phrases.notes: דברים כה:יג, read the same way as before: your purse will end up empty.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because of "a weight and a weight" (two different weights).
But "a perfect and just weight you shall have,"
phrases.notes: דברים כה:טו. He reads "you shall have" as a promise that you will have wealth.

phrases.english: "a perfect and just measure you shall have."

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ בְּכִיסְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's reading from step 7 and closes it with the positive promise
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unequal weights lead to an empty purse. Honest weights and measures bring wealth.

steps.title: Inspectors are appointed for measures but not for prices
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "יהיה לך" that the court appoints market inspectors to check measures, but not to control prices.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: "You shall have" teaches that we appoint market inspectors for measures, but we do not appoint market inspectors for prices.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא uses the words "יהיה לך" to teach that the court sets up inspectors who check that weights and measures are honest. It also says the court does not set up inspectors to control prices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק about honest weights is now read as an instruction to the community: make sure there are honest measures by appointing people to check them. The ברייתא limits this to measures. Prices are left to the sellers.

keyTerms.meaning: Market inspectors appointed to supervise the market

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"(You shall not) have":
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word לֹא in round brackets, so the ברייתא reads the positive "you shall have" from דברים 25:15.

phrases.english: teaches that we appoint market inspectors for measures,
but we do not appoint market inspectors for prices.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״(לֹא) יִהְיֶה לְךָ״ – מְלַמֵּד שֶׁמַּעֲמִידִין אֲגַרְדְּמִין לַמִּדּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic, market inspectors (the סימן's באגרדמין). It draws a rule for the community from the same honest-weights פסוק used in steps 3 to 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Market inspectors are appointed for measures, not for prices.

steps.title: שמואל sends קרנא to correct the house of the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The house of the נשיא appointed inspectors for both measures and prices, and שמואל sent קרנא to teach them the ברייתא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: The house of the נשיא appointed market inspectors both for measures and for prices. שמואל said to קרנא: Go out and teach them: We appoint market inspectors for measures, but we do not appoint market inspectors for prices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story. The house of the נשיא went further than the ברייתא and put inspectors on prices too, so שמואל told his student קרנא to go teach the correct rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story shows the ברייתא's rule being used in real life. שמואל holds like the ברייתא: checking prices is not the court's job. The story sets up what קרנא will do next.

phrases.english: The house of the Nasi appointed market inspectors
both for measures and for prices.
Shmuel said to Karna:
Go out and teach them:
We appoint market inspectors for measures,
but we do not appoint market inspectors for prices.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵי נְשִׂיאָה אוֹקִימוּ אֲגַרְדְּמִין בֵּין לַמִּדּוֹת בֵּין לַשְּׁעָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tells a story where the ברייתא's rule was applied.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל rules like the ברייתא: inspectors for measures only.

steps.title: קרנא teaches the opposite and is punished
steps.stepSummary: קרנא taught that inspectors are appointed for both measures and prices, and שמואל cursed him that a horn should grow in his eye, which happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went out and taught them: We appoint market inspectors both for measures and for prices. שמואל said to him: What is your name? קרנא. Let a horn come out in his eye. A horn came out in his eye.
steps.whatsHappening: קרנא did not teach what שמואל told him and instead taught that prices are supervised too. שמואל was upset, and his curse, a play on the name קרנא, came true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרנא changed his teacher's message, which is a serious thing. The punishment plays on his name: קרנא sounds like "horn." Why קרנא did this is asked in the next step and answered in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: He went out and taught them publicly

phrases.english: He went out and taught them:
We appoint market inspectors
both for measures and for prices.
He said to him: What is your name? Karna.
Let a horn come out in his eye.
phrases.notes: A play on his name: קַרְנָא also means "horn," here a growth on the eye.

phrases.english: A horn came out in his eye.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְפַק דְּרַשׁ לְהוּ: מַעֲמִידִין אֲגַרְדְּמִין בֵּין לַמִּדּוֹת בֵּין לַשְּׁעָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: קרנא does the opposite of what he was told.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קרנא taught that both measures and prices are supervised.

steps.title: Whose opinion did קרנא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which opinion קרנא was following when he taught differently from שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he, like whom did he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source קרנא relied on. It is setting up the next step, which gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A student of שמואל would not invent a rule out of nowhere. The גמרא assumes קרנא had an earlier opinion behind him and wants to find it.

phrases.english: And he, like whom did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיהוּ כְּמַאן סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind קרנא's teaching in the story.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which authority supports appointing inspectors for prices too.

steps.title: קרנא followed רבי יצחק: inspect prices too, because of cheaters
steps.stepSummary: קרנא held like רבי יצחק (quoted by רמי בר חמא), who says inspectors are appointed for both measures and prices because of cheaters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like that which רמי בר חמא said that רבי יצחק said: We appoint market inspectors both for measures and for prices, because of the cheaters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that קרנא followed רבי יצחק. רבי יצחק says prices are supervised too, to stop cheaters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So there are two opinions: the ברייתא and שמואל say measures only, and רבי יצחק says prices too. רבי יצחק's reason is to protect buyers from sellers who cheat on prices, not just on weights.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא and שמואל: inspectors check measures only. רבי יצחק, followed by קרנא: they check prices too, because of cheaters.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
phrases.english: Like that which Rami bar Chama said
that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
We appoint market inspectors
both for measures and for prices,
because of the cheaters.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: קרנא followed רבי יצחק, who supervises prices too because of cheaters.

steps.title: Weighing a litra, half a litra, and a quarter litra
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the seller uses a weight matching the amount asked for: a ליטרא, half a ליטרא, or a quarter ליטרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If he was asking from him a ליטרא, he weighs for him with a ליטרא weight. Half a ליטרא, he weighs for him with a half-ליטרא weight. A quarter ליטרא, he weighs for him with a quarter-ליטרא weight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא says that whatever amount the buyer asks for, a ליטרא, half, or a quarter, the seller weighs it with a weight of that size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This seems obvious, so the reader should expect the גמרא to ask what it is teaching. The list stops at a quarter ליטרא, which will turn out to matter.

keyTerms.meaning: A ליטרא, a unit of weight

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he was asking from him a litra,
he weighs for him with a litra weight.

phrases.aramaic: חֲצִי לִיטְרָא – שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ חֲצִי לִיטְרָא.
phrases.english: Half a litra: he weighs for him with a half-litra weight.

phrases.aramaic: רְבִיעַ לִיטְרָא – שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ רְבִיעַ לִיטְרָא.
phrases.english: A quarter litra: he weighs for him with a quarter-litra weight.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ לִיטְרָא שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ לִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the sizes of weights a seller uses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seller weighs with a weight equal to the amount asked for.

steps.title: What is this ברייתא teaching us?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what new point the ברייתא is making, since weighing with a matching weight seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it teaching us?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say something so simple. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes a ברייתא does not waste words. If the plain rule is obvious, there must be a hidden lesson.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the need for the ברייתא in step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The new point hidden in an obvious-seeming ברייתא.

steps.title: Weights are made only down to a quarter litra
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that weights are made only as small as a quarter ליטרא, and not smaller.
steps.simpleTranslation: That we make weights down to this size.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the lesson is in where the list stops. Weights are made down to a quarter ליטרא and no smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is not that you use a matching weight, but how small the weights go. Since the list stops at a quarter, a buyer cannot ask for a smaller weighing.

phrases.english: That we make weights down to this size.
phrases.notes: "This size" is the quarter litra, the last amount in the list.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּמְתַקְּנִינַן מַתְקָלֵי עַד הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The smallest weight made is a quarter ליטרא.

steps.title: Weighing three quarters of a litra in one go
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that three quarters of a ליטרא is not weighed as three separate quarters. It is weighed in one go: a ליטרא weight on one side, and a quarter weight with the meat on the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If he was asking from him three quarters of a ליטרא, he should not say to him: Weigh me three quarter-ליטרא weights one by one. Rather, he weighs with a ליטרא weight and places a quarter-ליטרא weight together with the meat.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא says the buyer may not ask for three separate quarter-ליטרא weighings. Instead the seller puts a ליטרא weight on one side and a quarter weight together with the meat on the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each separate weighing gives the buyer a little extra when the scale tips, so three weighings would cheat the seller. One weighing gives the exact amount: meat plus a quarter equals a ליטרא, so the meat is three quarters.
steps.whatToRemember: Weights go down only to a quarter ליטרא, and an amount like three quarters is weighed in one go, not piece by piece.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: הָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה רִבְעֵי לִיטְרָא,
phrases.english: If he was asking from him three quarters of a litra,
he should not say to him:
Weigh me three quarter-litras
one by one.
phrases.notes: Each separate weighing lets the scale tip a bit in the buyer's favor, so he would get extra.

phrases.english: Rather, he weighs with a litra weight,
and places a quarter-litra weight together with the meat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה רִבְעֵי לִיטְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the rule that the smallest weight is a quarter ליטרא and shows how to weigh an in-between amount.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three quarters of a ליטרא is weighed in one go: a ליטרא weight against the meat plus a quarter weight.

steps.title: Ten litra are weighed together with one tip of the scale
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that a buyer of ten ליטרא cannot demand ten separate weighings, each with its own tip of the scale. The seller weighs everything at once and gives one tip for the whole amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a buyer asked for ten ליטרא, he may not say, 'Weigh them for me one at a time and let the scale tip each time.' Instead, the seller weighs all of them at once and gives one tip of the scale for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא about fair weighing. This one stops a buyer from squeezing extra out of the seller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the scale tips toward the goods, the buyer gets a little more than the exact amount. If each ליטרא were weighed on its own, the buyer would get that small extra ten times. So the ברייתא says one weighing gets one tip, which protects the seller.

keyTerms.meaning: Litras, a unit of weight (plural of לִיטְרָא)
The tip of the scale, a slight extra weight given to the buyer
And let it tip (make the scale lean toward the goods)
All at once, in one go

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he was asking him for ten litra,
phrases.notes: The buyer is the one asking, and he is asking the seller.

phrases.english: he may not say to him:
Weigh for me one by one, and let it tip;
phrases.notes: 'Let it tip' means let the scale lean a bit toward the goods each time, so the buyer gets a little extra every time.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ כּוּלָּן בְּבַת אַחַת,
phrases.english: rather, he weighs all of them for him at once,
and gives one tip for all of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ מִמֶּנּוּ עֶשֶׂר לִיטְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like step 17, this rule says to weigh in one go instead of in separate pieces. Here the purpose is to stop extra tips of the scale from piling up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When many ליטרא are bought together, they are weighed together, and the buyer gets only one tip of the scale.

steps.title: Required measurements for different kinds of scales
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives the hanging height, the height above the ground, and the length of the rod and cord for four kinds of scales: a large scale, the scale of wool workers and glassmakers, the scale of a storekeeper or homeowner, and a small טורטני scale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: The center point of a scale must hang three טפחים down from where it is hung, the pans must be three טפחים above the ground, and its rod and cords must be twelve טפחים long. For wool workers and glassmakers: two טפחים down, two טפחים above the ground, and nine טפחים of rod and cord. For a storekeeper or homeowner: one טפח down, one טפח above the ground, and six טפחים of rod and cord. For a טורטני (a small scale): three finger-widths down and three finger-widths above the ground. As for its rod and cord, the תנא says, 'I do not know.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that sets fixed sizes for different kinds of scales. Each kind of scale gets its own measurements, from largest to smallest.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists four levels, and the sizes shrink at each level: 3/3/12 טפחים, then 2/2/9, then 1/1/6, then finger-widths. Every group except the first is tied to a kind of user. That gap sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The center point of a scale, where the beam hangs (literally 'the soul of the scale')
The rod (beam) and the cord that hold the pans
A handbreadth, a unit of length
A small scale, used for weighing gold and silver

steps.confusionAlert: Each kind of scale has two separate heights. 'Hanging in the air' is the distance from where the center point is hung down to the beam. 'High from the ground' is the distance of the pans above the floor. Don't mix them up.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
The center point of a scale –
hangs in the air three handbreadths,
and is high off the ground three handbreadths,
and its rod and cord
are twelve handbreadths.
And that of wool workers and of glassmakers –
hangs in the air two handbreadths,
and is high off the ground two handbreadths,
and its rod and cord are nine handbreadths.
And that of a storekeeper and of a homeowner –
hangs in the air one handbreadth,
and is high off the ground one handbreadth,
and its rod and cord are six handbreadths.
And that of a small scale (turtani) –
hangs in the air three finger-widths,
and is high off the ground three finger-widths,
and its rod and cord, I do not know.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נֶפֶשׁ מֹאזְנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The topic shifts from how to weigh to how the scale itself must be built.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each kind of scale has fixed measurements for its hanging height, its height off the ground, and its rod and cord, and the sizes get smaller as the scale gets smaller.

steps.title: Who uses the first, largest scale?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא named the users of every scale except the first one. So the גמרא asks what that first scale is for.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that first scale, what is it used for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the ברייתא never said who uses the first, largest scale. It asks this question, and the answer will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every other scale in the ברייתא is tied to a kind of user: wool workers and glassmakers, a storekeeper or homeowner, and the טורטני. The first scale is left without one. This is a real request for information, not a challenge to the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: That first one (the first scale listed)
Of what? What is it used for?

phrases.english: But that first one –
phrases.notes: He means the first, biggest scale, the one with the twelve-handbreadth rod and cord.

phrases.english: what is it for?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָךְ קַמַּיְיתָא – דְּמַאי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a detail that the ברייתא in step 19 left out.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of user or goods the first, largest scale in the ברייתא is meant for.
